questions.q: Which piece of hardware loses its contents the instant the power goes off?
options: Storage (SSD/HDD)
The network interface
RAM
The CPU
questions.explain: RAM is fast, temporary workspace. Whatever is in it disappears when power is lost, which is why storage exists for anything that needs to persist.

questions.q: What is the CPU's job in a computer?
options: Permanently storing files and programs
Executing instructions, one at a time, extremely fast
Connecting the machine to a network
Deciding which application a user prefers
questions.explain: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the chip that actually executes instructions, billions of times per second.

questions.q: Which of the following is a core job of an operating system?
options: Designing the user interface of a specific application
Scheduling which program gets to use the CPU and for how long
Writing the retailer's product catalog
Replacing the need for physical hardware entirely
questions.explain: Process scheduling — deciding which program uses the CPU and when — is one of the operating system's core responsibilities, alongside memory management and device/file access.

questions.q: In the three-layer model (hardware, OS, software), how does an application like a browser reach the hardware?
options: It talks to the hardware directly, bypassing the operating system
It runs through the operating system, which manages the hardware on its behalf
It only works if there is no operating system installed
It becomes part of the hardware once installed
questions.explain: Applications run through the operating system. They never talk to hardware directly — the OS mediates that access for every program.

questions.q: At Northbridge Retail, checkout terminals run a point-of-sale application on a Linux-based OS, while corporate laptops run productivity software on Windows. What does this illustrate?
options: Linux and Windows are incompatible with the three-layer model
The same hardware/OS/application layering applies even when the specific OS and software choices differ
Point-of-sale systems don't need an operating system
Windows laptops don't have a hardware layer
questions.explain: The three-layer model — hardware, operating system, application — holds regardless of which specific OS or application is chosen at each layer.
